newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin annuls unpopular tax decree.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin annuls unpopular tax decree.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Friday annulled a controversial decree from last month, which set thorough controls on incomes, including taxes on all bank operations of private persons.

The decree, which was never implemented, was intended to impose taxes on bank operations of all private account-holders, because many domestic companies paid their employees in the form of interest on their bank deposits, to avoid income tax.

But the decree, which would have resulted in people being taxed on withdrawals from their accounts, applied also pensioners and other low-income people, led many individuals to withdraw all their money from the bank.
It was widely condemned by business leaders and bankers.
An official of the presidential press service told Reuters the unpopular decree had been abolished in full, the decision coming into effect starting September 6.
